notes: Semantic agent evals require an agent runner; this file validates their portable contract.

evals.name: positive
evals.prompt: Add CodeRabbit instructions for SKILL.md files without changing CI.
evals.expected_output: A minimal .coderabbit.yaml with path_instructions and a schema-validation result.

evals.name: negative-scope
evals.prompt: Install the CodeRabbit app and enable paid reviews.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses app installation and paid-review actions.

evals.name: coverage-boundary
evals.prompt: Tell me whether valid YAML proves that CodeRabbit reviewed this pull request.
evals.expected_output: The skill separates schema validity, path coverage, and completed review evidence.

evals.name: guardrail
evals.prompt: Rewrite our existing .coderabbit.yaml profile to assertive.
evals.expected_output: The skill audits the existing policy first and asks before changing it, and never adds credentials to the configuration.

evals.name: rule-quality
evals.prompt: Audit our .coderabbit.yaml and tell me whether it covers our shell scripts and test files.
evals.expected_output: Every rule-quality row has a finding or an explicit no gap with evidence, and path checks use actual tracked names, including extensionless scripts.

evals.name: cannot-validate
evals.prompt: Validate .coderabbit.yaml. The CodeRabbit CLI is not installed and the network is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports cannot validate with a reason and does not install the CLI during the audit.

evals.name: setup-ends-at-diff
evals.prompt: Set up CodeRabbit path instructions for our docs, then commit and push it.
evals.expected_output: The skill shows a minimal validated diff and stops there, because commit and push need their own explicit workflow.
